questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on his right hand with a black eschar and surrounding gelatinous edema. He had contact with animal hides 5 days ago. Gram stain shows large gram-positive bacilli in chains. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax presents with a painless necrotic ulcer with a black eschar and characteristic gelatinous non-pitting edema after contact with infected animal products. Bacillus anthracis is a large gram-positive bacillus forming chains.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. What is the most appropriate first-line topical treatment?
questions.exp: Impetigo due to S. aureus is best treated with topical mupirocin 2% as first-line therapy with excellent activity including MRSA.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with annular scaly plaque on the scalp with alopecia. KOH shows ectothrix hyphae. Hairs fluoresce bright green under Wood's lamp. Which dermatophyte is responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix tinea capitis and fluoresces bright green under Wood's lamp due to pteridine metabolites. Trichophyton species cause endothrix and do NOT fluoresce.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male develops rapidly progressive black necrotic plaques on his nose and hard palate after DKA. CT shows bony erosion. Drug of choice?
questions.exp: Rhinocerebral mucormycosis requires liposomal amphotericin B. Voriconazole has NO activity against Mucorales. Surgical debridement is also essential.

questions.q: A 16-year-old has grouped vesicles on the lips recurring each few months triggered by sunlight. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. In which ganglion does HSV-1 establish latency?
questions.exp: HSV-1 establishes latency in the trigeminal ganglion. On reactivation it travels anterograde to perioral skin. Tzanck smear with multinucleated giant cells confirms herpetic infection.

questions.q: A 30-year-old has skin-colored dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on the trunk. Which histological finding is pathognomonic?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (MCV, poxvirus) produces Henderson-Paterson bodies: large eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in keratinocytes. Cowdry type A bodies in HSV/VZV; owl-eye in CMV; koilocytes in HPV.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male has a painless indurated genital ulcer with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. VDRL is negative. Best diagnostic test?
opts: Giemsa stain of lymph node aspirate
questions.exp: Primary syphilis: VDRL frequently negative early. Dark-field microscopy demonstrating motile Treponema pallidum from ulcer exudate is the gold-standard direct test.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman has painful soft genital ulcers with tender fluctuant inguinal buboes. Gram stain: gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' pattern. Treatment?
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi): Azithromycin 1g single dose is a first-line CDC-recommended treatment. Benzathine penicillin treats syphilis. Doxycycline 21 days treats LGV.

questions.q: A 40-year-old has hypopigmented anesthetic patches, thickened peripheral nerves, and slit-skin smear showing 1+ bacilli. WHO treatment regimen?
opts: Multibacillary MDT for 12 months (rifampicin + dapsone + clofazimine)
questions.exp: Any positive smear = multibacillary leprosy regardless of lesion count. MB-MDT: rifampicin + clofazimine monthly + dapsone + clofazimine daily for 12 months.

questions.q: A lepromatous leprosy patient on MDT develops painful red nodular lesions, fever, joint pain, and neuritis. Biopsy: neutrophilic infiltrate with foam cells. Immunological mechanism?
questions.exp: ENL (Type 2 lepra reaction) is mediated by immune complex deposition (Type III HSR). Treatment: thalidomide (drug of choice) or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman has tense bullae on flexural areas. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the DEJ. Target antigen?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid: DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at BMZ. Autoantibodies target BP180 (NC16A domain) and BP230 in the hemidesmosome. Desmoglein 3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris.

questions.q: A 35-year-old has flaccid bullae, oral erosions, and positive Nikolsky's sign. DIF: intercellular IgG in 'chicken-wire' pattern. Autoantigen targeted in mucosal-dominant disease?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris with mucosal dominance targets desmoglein 3 (Dsg3). Both Dsg1 and Dsg3 antibodies present when skin and mucosa affected. Dsg1 alone targeted in pemphigus foliaceus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman has violaceous papules on wrists with Wickham's striae. Biopsy: band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ, sawtooth rete ridges, civatte bodies. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lichen planus: 4 P's (Purple, Polygonal, Pruritic Papules), Wickham's striae, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ, civatte bodies, hypergranulosis, sawtooth rete ridges.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has butterfly rash, oral ulcers, ANA 1:640, anti-dsDNA positive, and proteinuria. Which cutaneous finding in SLE best correlates with renal involvement?
questions.exp: Vasculitis in SLE (palpable purpura, digital infarcts) reflects immune complex deposition in vessels and correlates strongly with systemic disease activity and renal involvement.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male has a pearly papule with telangiectasias on his nose. Biopsy: basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact. Most appropriate treatment?
opts: Wide local excision with 2 cm margins
questions.exp: Nodular BCC on the nose (H-zone) is best treated with Mohs surgery (~99% cure rate, maximal tissue conservation). Imiquimod is for superficial BCC only.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer has a rapidly growing dome-shaped nodule with central keratin crater on the forearm over 6 weeks, beginning to involute. Biopsy: well-differentiated squamous cells with glassy cytoplasm and buttressing architecture. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma: rapidly growing, self-resolving lesion with central keratin crater. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous cells with glassy cytoplasm and buttressing architecture. Treated by excision.

questions.q: A patient started on carbamazepine 3 weeks ago has fever, mucosal erosions, and blisters covering 25% BSA with positive Nikolsky's sign. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: SJS <10% BSA, TEN >30%, SJS/TEN overlap 10-30%. This case: 25% BSA = SJS/TEN overlap following carbamazepine. SSSS spares mucosa. Erythema multiforme has targetoid lesions and minimal detachment.

questions.q: A patient on allopurinol develops fever, lymphadenopathy, facial edema, morbilliform rash with 30% eosinophilia, and elevated LFTs 6 weeks after starting. Diagnosis and first step?
opts: DRESS syndrome — immediately stop the offending drug
Serum sickness — stop drug and antihistamines
Drug-induced lupus — stop drug and monitor
questions.exp: DRESS presents 2-8 weeks after drug with fever, lymphadenopathy, facial edema, eosinophilia, and organ involvement (liver most common). Immediate drug cessation first, then systemic corticosteroids. HHV-6 reactivation implicated.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery for a facial BCC, which staining technique is used intraoperatively to evaluate surgical margins?
questions.exp: Mohs surgery uses horizontal (en face) frozen sections stained with H&E to examine 100% of surgical margins in real time, allowing immediate re-excision of positive margins.

questions.q: A patient with melasma is planned for a superficial chemical peel. Which is the gold-standard agent for melasma with the best evidence?
questions.exp: Glycolic acid (AHA, 20-70%) is the most studied agent for melasma. TCA 35% achieves medium-depth peel. Phenol carries cardiotoxicity risk. Jessner's + TCA 35% is for photoaging.

questions.q: A 20-year-old has erythematous silvery-scaled plaques on knees, elbows, and scalp with positive Auspitz sign. Biopsy: parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses, elongated rete ridges. Which cytokine axis primarily drives psoriasis?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is driven by the IL-23/IL-17 axis. IL-23 drives Th17 cells producing IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22, causing keratinocyte proliferation and Munro microabscesses. Biologics targeting IL-17 and IL-23 are highly effective.

questions.q: A 16-year-old with nodular acne is started on oral isotretinoin. Most critical monitoring parameter at 4-6 weeks?
questions.exp: Isotretinoin causes hypertriglyceridemia (up to 25%) and elevated liver enzymes. Fasting lipids and LFTs mandatory at baseline and 4-6 weeks. Severe hypertriglyceridemia (>800 mg/dL) can cause pancreatitis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman has recurrent wheals and angioedema for 8 weeks, unresponsive to antihistamines, with positive ASST. What does this indicate?
opts: IgG autoantibodies to FcεRI or IgE — autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria
IgE sensitization to an unidentified allergen
questions.exp: Positive ASST indicates autoimmune CSU: IgG autoantibodies target FcεRIα on mast cells or IgE causing allergen-independent degranulation. This subset responds well to omalizumab.

questions.q: A 50-year-old has a 3 cm ulcerated nodule on the calf with satellite nodules ascending along lymphatics after a rose-thorn prick. Causative organism?
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis: lymphocutaneous pattern after thorn inoculation. Sporothrix schenckii is a thermally dimorphic fungus. Treatment: itraconazole 200 mg/day for 3-6 months, or SSKI.

questions.q: A child has moth-eaten alopecia, snail-track oral ulcers, maculopapular rash on palms and soles. VDRL 1:64 and TPHA positive. Stage and treatment?
opts: Secondary syphilis — benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
Primary syphilis — doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
Tertiary syphilis — benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM weekly x 3
Latent syphilis — doxycycline 100 mg for 28 days
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis: maculopapular rash (palms/soles classic), moth-eaten alopecia, snail-track ulcers, strongly reactive VDRL. Treatment: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose.

questions.q: A 55-year-old HIV-positive male (CD4 120) has violaceous plaques on lower limbs, oral mucosa, and a pulmonary nodule. Biopsy: spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces. First-line treatment for extensive disease?
questions.exp: AIDS-associated Kaposi's sarcoma (HHV-8) with extensive/visceral disease: ART plus liposomal doxorubicin (first-line for advanced KS). Topical alitretinoin only for localized cutaneous lesions.

questions.q: During dermoscopy you observe atypical pigment network, irregular blotches, and a blue-white veil. What does the blue-white veil histologically correspond to?
opts: Sheets of melanophages in fibrotic dermis overlying confluent melanocyte nests
Dilated blood vessels in papillary dermis
Confluent melanin in the basal layer only
questions.exp: Blue-white veil: acanthotic epidermis overlying sheets of melanophages in fibrotic dermis covering confluent melanocyte nests. Major dermoscopic criterion for melanoma.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman has hypopigmented macules on the upper trunk that fail to tan. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs'. Mechanism of hypopigmentation in pityriasis versicolor?
opts: Malassezia produces azelaic acid which inhibits tyrosinase
Direct melanocyte destruction by fungal hyphae
Blocking of UVB penetration by pseudohyphae
questions.exp: Malassezia metabolizes fatty acids to azelaic acid which competitively inhibits tyrosinase, reducing melanin synthesis. Treatment: topical selenium sulfide, ketoconazole shampoo, or oral itraconazole.

questions.q: A 4-year-old develops widespread superficial blistering with large denuded wet areas. Mucous membranes are spared. Nikolsky's sign positive. Biopsy shows cleavage in the granular layer. Pathomechanism?
opts: Exfoliative toxins A/B from S. aureus cleave desmoglein 1 at the granular layer
questions.exp: SSSS: exfoliative toxins A and B from S. aureus phage group II cleave desmoglein 1 at the granular layer. Mucosa is spared (Dsg3 maintains integrity). Treatment: antistaphylococcal antibiotics.

questions.q: A 40-year-old has extremely pruritic grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, and buttocks. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papilla tips. He has celiac disease. Treatment?
opts: Dapsone for rapid relief plus strict gluten-free diet
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis: granular IgA at dermal papilla tips is pathognomonic. Dapsone provides rapid symptomatic relief; gluten-free diet is the definitive long-term treatment. Check G6PD before dapsone.
